column5: SIWC execute, stream, compact, WebSocket and image requests, the missing-token failure and the selective and dual refresh are ported (Go-recorded request goldens). The file-lock refresh (L1150) is ported as one transaction under the credential lock, owned apart from the caller: a refresh waits for the lock, adopts a partition another process rotated on disk without refreshing it again, spends the file's tokens over a stale snapshot (A→B→C), forces a refresh after a 401 only while the adopted partition still holds the rejected access token, after a grant writes the refreshed partitions onto the file as read again under the lock (Go matchesBaselineOrAfter over the snapshot, the locked file and the result; other fields, such as disabled, as the file holds them; values as Go's float64 decode), and only then admits the result to the store as Go updateInternal does: a re-registered ID is refused and a credential whose version moved or whose tokens changed, past every partition (CanApplyTo), discards the refresh without side effects; an admitted one is written again over the file with legacy keys renamed (PersistCodexAuthFile) and published with its proxy; an adopt-only refresh reaches the file only when admitted. A failed save is logged and the patch over memory published, a removed file written again from memory, as Go's manager does. At shutdown, a refresh still waiting for the lock gives up and one holding it finishes. Plugin-virtual Codex credentials refresh in memory (docs/DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md). A corrupt, emptied or vanished file fails. The Home-mode SIWC refresh (L1071) is not ported: Go's server never reaches it (Home mode loads no local credentials, and a dispatched Codex auth is neither prepared nor refreshed after a 401).

Go clears only double-quoted key styles on a v8 save, so a double-quoted "<<" merges a mapping or fails on a scalar after the next save, a single-quoted '<<' stays a plain key, and an unknown section archived before the save never merges. A JSON body sent to /config.yaml is the same gap (Go 422, Rust 400). Other JSON management bodies match Go: << stays literal through the root-shape check and the update, then the completed candidate is expanded, so keys already present win (manage_go.rs config_writes merge_keys_in_json_bodies).

column5: Suite changed since 6fecc6e; existing fixtures do not establish every v8.0.35 assertion. See the current Go declarations in checklist.md. Addon follows Go: only errors with Headers() (WebSocket error frames, stream bootstrap failures) hand headers to the client. authUnavailableError and modelCooldownError also implement Headers() (Retry-After); Rust writes that Retry-After whether or not passthrough is on, as Go's SafeResponseHeaders does. Framing headers in an Addon are dropped, where Go copies them (an upstream Content-Length can cut Go's error body). JSON validity of a 400 error body differs from Go's json.Valid: openai_body (serde_json) wraps "\uD800", 1e400 and nesting deeper than 128 levels in an OpenAI envelope as message text, where Go compacts and passes them through; the Responses WebSocket error_body (gjson valid) accepts those as Go does but has no 10,000-level depth limit, so it passes through nesting Go wraps. Duplicate keys behave the same.

Only refresh_interval schedules a background refresh (Go shouldRefresh without a lead). LastRefreshedAt and NextRefreshAfter are kept in memory per credential and registered with every change to the credential set, by Go's registration rule (prepareCoreAuthForModelRegistration): a credential registered again (an edit, a reload, a management change) keeps them while it and the one it replaces are both enabled, and otherwise (disabled or enabled again) takes the ones it is registered with, no LastRefreshedAt and the NextRefreshAfter its plugin parsed for it with that registration; a host.auth.save's auth takes those of the registered auth it replaces (Go findExistingAuthForSave and preserveExistingAuthState, unset ones included and under another ID too), else its own parsed one, once the manager registers it; a disabled saved credential ends with its own (the registration Go's watcher makes of the written file, DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md); a credential that leaves the set loses them (Manager.Remove), so one registered afresh, from the same file or another, starts from its own registration, and a refresh that started under an earlier registration of its ID is refused by the shared refresh writer, for every provider, before it merges or saves anything, and records nothing (Go's RegistrationEpoch: a registration number set when the ID enters the set and kept while it is registered again); a committed refresh's LastRefreshedAt is published with the credential, and a failed one reads the current credential; the startup load, made before plugins parse auth files, is provisional: the background refresh leaves it alone, and the first plugin-aware load registers each credential with its parsed NextRefreshAfter as Go's first load does, even when nothing else changed; a management status change registers without asking the plugin (DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md); a failed or unsaved refresh from any trigger sets 5 min (capped at the current token's expiry, and not extended by the built-in refresh backoff), a refresh that leaves the credential due sets 30 s, and a refresh an unrelated edit made a no-op still records LastRefreshedAt. The saved document carries the response's disabled state and Go's merged proxy_url, which the running credential takes with it (a concurrent edit that wins the document wins both); a response that changes the provider or ID is refused, and prefix and attribute changes wait for the next load (DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md). Built-in providers keep their own refresh, compat-named ones included (DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md). column5: As in Go's buildAuthsFromFileData, the save asks the plugin auth provider for the file's type first, holding no lock: a failed parse fails the save before the write; each parsed auth's metadata is normalized before one auth inherits the file's other fields, and without its own ID it keeps the ID of the file's credential (as a built-in save does); only Go's save-time rules apply from the decoded file (priority, weight, prefix, proxy URL, disabled state and the auth's headers; the watcher applies the file's excluded models and aliases when it next parses it), and JSON null decodes to no fields as in Go; the parsed credentials replace the file's other ones (upsertAuthRecordsForPath). As in Manager.persist, only one auth that is neither runtime-only nor plugin-virtual and whose storage builds is persisted, and such an auth records its disabled state in its metadata first (FileTokenStore.Save); otherwise the file keeps the saved bytes and the auth is still registered. The save writes and registers under the management disk lock. Deliberate differences (DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md): a save from inside the same plugin's auth.parse of the file, on the parsing thread, writes without parsing again (Go recurses without bound); one from another thread while that plugin parses the file for a save is refused; a parsed auth naming another file is refused.

Start, callback, exchange, commit, cancellation, expiry, the legacy-callback refusal and the v8 list summary follow Go. The start reads its target under the management disk lock, as Go holds its commit gate (management::siwc::tests::a_bind_reads_its_target_only_under_the_disk_lock); the callback compares the percent-decoded path exactly; the commit refuses a file whose account changed since the start. The commit takes the credential's refresh lock, so an outer-token refresh in flight finishes first, even when its caller was cancelled (runtime::tests::a_cancelled_refresh_holds_the_preparation_lock_through_its_commit), and a cancelled binding keeps the lock until its commit returns (management::siwc::tests::a_cancelled_binding_holds_the_preparation_lock_through_its_commit), and both its rotated tokens and the binding are kept; Go reaches the same result by merging scoped patches. Not reproduced: Go's registration-epoch check (a target deleted and re-imported during the exchange is bound if its file, provider and account still match; M5-0247). After a binding is saved, an enabled target's unauthorized cooldowns are cleared, as Go's BindCodexSIWC does: model keys match a 401 or "unauthorized" in the error (Go's status-message check), the credential-wide key only Go's isUnauthorizedError. A quota block still live under a 401 stays blocked until the same time, as a quota cooldown with the quota's own status and reason (quota, cloudflare challenge or credential_quota), because Go keeps ModelState.Quota when recording a 401; the error becomes that reason only when it names "unauthorized", as Go rewrites only such a status message. The block is kept in memory beside the 401 and survives a restore while serving (save-cooldown-status turned on or moved), but not a restart, because saved records hold the 401 alone. Covered by the bound-step cooldown checks in siwc_binding_flows_follow_go and scheduler::tests clear_unauthorized_matches_go_per_key_kind, a_401_over_a_live_quota_keeps_the_quota_through_recovery and a_quota_under_a_401_keeps_its_kind_through_restore_and_recovery. Not covered: saving the cleared cooldowns (persist_cooldowns is called, but the integration test runs with cooldown saving off). Differences from Go: Go clears LastError, so its management output for the kept quota has no http_status, while Rust still reports the quota's status; Go also matches the error code "unauthorized", which cooldowns do not keep. In a live bounded window, a 401 whose body does not say "unauthorized" leaves the window as it is, which blocks the same as Go. Go's rejected access token has no Rust counterpart, because a 401 retry keys on the credential revision the binding replaces. Requests do not use the bound tokens yet: use_siwc in the Codex executor belongs to the executor work.

column5: The budget cases use Go's codexOverloadEvent (Go's own split-budget cases send server_overloaded, which never fails over) plus a within-budget control that fails over. Not replayed: the two clock-driven cases (Rust's bootstrap has no injectable clock) and the [DONE] log assertion. The byte budget counts each line's Codex-format output as its translated size. That equals Go's translator output for Codex clients and for Responses-client events the translator leaves unchanged; Go's Responses translator inserts a missing response.model, so such events count more bytes in Go (a 524,250-byte comment, then data: {"type":"response.in_progress"}, then the overload fails over in Rust and releases in Go). For Claude and Chat clients the count is approximate. Both differences matter only when the cumulative total straddles 1 MiB. Transport-level, not ported: the shared whole-event framer rejects an unfinished event over 16 MiB, below Go's 50 MiB line limit, and does not reject a complete frame over 50 MiB; releasing bootstrap while the upstream is mid-assembly, and processing a terminal line before its blank line, wait for the event delimiter. A Codex-specific incremental line reader would close these.

No session, an idle pooled socket and a disabled credential write nothing; a turn reading on the socket gets the interrupt byte for byte. A failed or timed-out interrupt write drops the socket (docs/DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md, write bound).

The shared reader (codex_ws::read_loop, also xAI's) records completed, done, incomplete and failed response IDs per socket before delivery; the socket's state is read after the account check. Replayed for all four terminal types, an unknown ID and a lost socket.

column5: Added since 6fecc6e. Rust has no per-file snapshot: each reload re-reads the auth folder, so a credential is removed only when its file is gone or no longer holds it. An incomplete read is recorded by the hash of what the scan read, as Go invalidates its cached hash, so a write completed after the scan is reloaded (src/watching.rs the_watcher_records_what_its_reload_read_not_what_it_observed). Go's cases are not ported one by one.

column3: crates/cpa-server/src/watching.rs reload_config and keep_incomplete; src/watching.rs incomplete_auth_writes_keep_the_credential_until_the_file_is_valid_json, a_file_completed_after_the_scan_keeps_its_credential, an_unreadable_file_drops_its_credential, a_file_replaced_by_a_special_file_link_drops_its_credential, a_removed_and_recreated_file_keeps_its_credential
column5: Added since 6fecc6e. A whole-file removal is decided from the folder at reload time, so a delete event that outlives a re-created file cannot remove it. Go's queued per-ID delete mechanism needs no counterpart: each reload reconciles against disk, the store consumers reread paths, Git guards watcher removals, and cpa-home has no auth-dir mirror. Only a file read successfully as empty or invalid JSON keeps its credential. Go's REMOVE path (service_auth.go shouldSkipFileAuthDelete) also keeps it when the stat fails with an error other than not-found, when the single-file snapshot fails (including a plugin parse error under StrictFileParsing), or when the snapshot has no valid IDs; here a stat or read failure, {}, or valid JSON that synthesis rejects all drop it, which matches Go's full scan but not its REMOVE path. The scan counts only entries that are or link to regular files, the watcher's rule, so a file replaced by a link to /dev/null drops its credential at once; Go would read it as empty and keep the credential until the REMOVE event. Go's cases are not ported one by one.

Go 1631875b records the parsed config's SourceHash; watching.rs reload_config returns the hashes of the bytes it read (None for a failed read, as the observation records it) and record() keeps those as applied, so a write after the read (including a restore of bytes observed earlier) is reloaded when next observed. When the read differs from the observation the hash cache is dropped, so a stale cached hash cannot reload every tick. Go's concurrent-reload case has no Rust interleaving: one watcher task reloads, under the disk lock that saves hold.
Go 94d1a9a0, 1a28c61e. The plugin-parser cases (KeepsPluginExcludedModelsWithoutFileRules and the plugin case of KeepsCredentialWithInvalid) wait for plugin auth.parse.

column5: Go feb63984. Codex only. Not ported (post-replay): the background refresh after a 401 for other providers, Claude's included (Go scheduleUnauthorizedRefresh); isCredentialBlocked for unauthorized and expired tokens; the credential-wide scheduler upsert after a 401. A Codex credential whose refresh keeps failing retries forever under the refresh backoff (60 s doubling to 1800 s for invalid_grant, else 300 s), parked with the terminal state; Go's background worker passes no failed token, so its terminal branch is the inline one. Only the first 401 per revision sets the time, narrower than Go's NextRefreshAfter.IsZero(): Go also keeps an existing reservation, and a metadata-only revision change restarts the rule here. The 96 h lead makes every Codex credential with 96 h or less left due at once on deploy, drained through the refresh workers without jitter; the no-expiry last_refresh fallback also moves from 24 h to 96 h.
